questions.question: In whose court is the celebrated Sanskrit poet Kalidasa believed to have flourished?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa**, widely regarded as the greatest poet and dramatist in the **Sanskrit** language, is historically associated with the court of **Chandragupta II**.
 
• He was celebrated as one of the **Navaratnas** (Nine Gems), a group of nine distinguished scholars and artists who graced the royal court of the **Gupta Empire**.
 
• **Chandragupta II**, who assumed the prestigious title of **Vikramaditya**, ruled from approximately **380 CE to 415 CE**, marking the peak of the **Gupta Golden Age**.
 
• The poet's works, including the world-renowned drama **Abhijnanashakuntalam** and epic poems like **Meghaduta** and **Kumarasambhava**, reflect the cultural sophistication and religious harmony of the **Gupta era**.
 
• While the primary capital was **Pataliputra**, **Chandragupta II** maintained a secondary capital at **Ujjain**, which became a significant center for literary and scientific advancements where **Kalidasa** flourished.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• Often referred to as the **Napoleon of India** by historian **V.A. Smith** due to his extensive military conquests.
 
• He was a versatile genius and a poet himself, earning the title **Kaviraja** (King of Poets).
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta**:
 
 
• The son and successor of **Chandragupta II**, his reign saw the establishment of the famous **Nalanda University**.
 
• He was a worshiper of **Lord Kartikeya** and performed the **Ashvamedha** sacrifice to assert his imperial authority.
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta**:
 
 
• Recognized as the last great **Gupta Emperor**, he is famous for successfully defending the empire against the **Hunas** (Huns).
 
• His achievements are inscribed on the **Bhitari Pillar** and the **Junagarh Rock**.

questions.question: Which is the largest metropolitan city by population as per Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011** data, **Mumbai** (as an Urban Agglomeration) was the most populous metropolitan city in India, with a total population of approximately **18,414,288**.
 
• The **Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR)** encompasses the **Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM)** and several surrounding satellite towns like **Thane**, **Navi Mumbai**, and **Kalyan-Dombivli**.
 
• The city has a massive population density, often exceeding **20,000 persons per square kilometer** in its core urban districts, making it one of the most densely populated regions globally.
 
• The demographic growth in **Mumbai** is largely driven by its status as the **Economic Capital of India**, housing the headquarters of major financial institutions like the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, **BSE**, and **NSE**.
 
• In the hierarchy of Indian cities during the **2011 Census**, **Mumbai** held the top rank, followed by the National Capital Territory of **Delhi** and the city of **Kolkata**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi**:

 
 
• As per the **2011 Census**, it was the second largest metropolitan city with a population of about **16,314,838**.
 
• It serves as the **National Capital Territory (NCT)** and is a major hub for administrative, political, and commercial activities in **North India**.
 
 
 
• **Kolkata**:
 
 
• It ranked third among metropolitan cities with a population of approximately **14,112,536**.
 
• It was the former capital of the **British Raj** and remains the primary economic and cultural center of **East India**.
 
 
 
• **Chennai**:
 
 
• The city recorded a population of about **8,696,010** in its metropolitan area, placing it fourth among the major metros.
 
• Often referred to as the **Detroit of Asia**, it is a critical center for the **automobile industry** and health services.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011 Overview**:
 
 
• This was the **15th National Census** of India and the **7th** after independence.
 
• The Census defined a **Metropolitan City** or **Mega City** as one having a population of **4 million** or more, while a **Million-Plus City** is one with at least **1 million** residents.
 
• The census was conducted under the leadership of **C. Chandramouli**, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.

questions.question: What is the annual allocation under PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana which was approved in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 30000 crores**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** (PM-DDKY) is a major agricultural reform initiative officially approved by the **Union Cabinet** in **July 2025** to bolster the rural economy and ensure long-term **food security**.
 
• The scheme has been granted a substantial annual allocation of **Rs. 30,000 crores**, aimed at providing a comprehensive safety net and growth framework for the **farming community** across India.
 
• This budgetary provision is specifically designed to facilitate **technological upgrades** in farming, such as the adoption of **precision agriculture**, **AI-driven crop monitoring**, and the deployment of **agricultural drones**.
 
• The primary focus of the **Rs. 30,000 crores** fund is to support **small and marginal farmers** who constitute the majority of the Indian agricultural workforce, helping them transition toward **high-value crops** and **sustainable farming** practices.
 
• The scheme integrates various sub-components including **soil health management**, **subsidized quality seeds**, and **direct benefit transfers** (DBT) for essential farm inputs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic Objectives of PM-DDKY**:

 
 
• **Crop Diversification**: Encouraging farmers to shift from water-intensive monocultures to **nutri-cereals**, pulses, and oilseeds to improve ecological balance.
 
• **Post-Harvest Infrastructure**: A portion of the **Rs. 30,000 crores** is earmarked for building **cold storage facilities** and **warehouse hubs** at the village level to reduce wastage.
 
• **Irrigation Efficiency**: Strengthening the **Per Drop More Crop** mission by providing incentives for **drip and sprinkler irrigation** systems.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Monitoring**:
 
 
• The **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** serves as the lead agency for the execution of this scheme, utilizing the **Digital General Platform** for real-time tracking of fund utilization.
 
• The allocation is part of a broader vision of **Viksit Bharat 2047**, aiming to double the share of agriculture in the **Gross Value Added (GVA)** through systematic financial injections and **policy reforms**.
 
• Special emphasis is placed on **Aspirational Districts** and the **North-Eastern Region** to bridge the infrastructure gap in the primary sector.

questions.question: In which year was the Mazagon Dock taken over by the government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1960**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)**, situated in **Mumbai**, was originally incorporated as a public limited company in **1934**.
 
• The **Government of India** took over the management of the dockyard in **April 1960** to enhance the nation’s **self-reliance** in defense production.
 
• Following the nationalization, the shipyard was placed under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Defence**, specifically the **Department of Defence Production**.
 
• The primary objective of the takeover was to transform the facility into a premier **warship building yard** capable of meeting the strategic requirements of the **Indian Navy**.
 
• Since **1960**, MDL has transitioned from a small ship repair yard into a sophisticated **Defence Public Sector Undertaking (DPSU)** that constructs **destroyers**, **frigates**, and **submarines**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Significance and Growth:**

 
 
• Before the **1960** acquisition, the yard was owned by the **British India Steam Navigation Company** and the **Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Company**.
 
• In **1968**, the yard launched **INS Nilgiri**, the first **Leander-class frigate** built indigenously in India, which was commissioned in **1972**.
 
• MDL is currently involved in high-profile projects such as **Project 15B** (Visakhapatnam-class destroyers) and **Project 17A** (Nilgiri-class stealth frigates).
 
• It is also the site for **Project 75**, responsible for the construction of **Scorpene-class (Kalvari-class) submarines** through a technology transfer agreement with **Naval Group, France**.
 
• The facility remains one of the few shipyards in the world capable of building both conventional **submarines** and heavy **surface combatants**.

questions.question:
Which pressure belt is being talked about in the information given below?

"This pressure belt is found between 30°N to 35°N latitude and this is also known as horse latitude."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sub-tropical high pressure belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sub-tropical high pressure belt** is located in both hemispheres between approximately **30°N to 35°N** and **30°S to 35°S** latitudes.
 
• This belt is also famously known as the **Horse Latitudes** due to the calm winds and high pressure that historically stalled sailing ships.
 
• The formation of this belt is primarily due to the **subsidence** of air; air that rises at the **Equator** (Hadley Cell) cools as it moves poleward and descends at these latitudes, creating **high-pressure** conditions at the surface.
 
• Characterized by **anticyclonic** conditions, this region experiences light winds, clear skies, and low humidity, which is why most of the world's **hot deserts** (like the Sahara and Arabian deserts) are located along these latitudes.
 
• The term **Horse Latitudes** originated because sailors, when becalmed for long periods, had to throw **horses** overboard to conserve drinking water for the crew.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equatorial Low Pressure Belt**:

 
 
• Located between **5°N and 5°S** latitudes.
 
• Known as the **Doldrums**, it is a zone of convergence for trade winds and intense solar heating.
 
 
 
• **Sub-polar Low Pressure Belt**:
 
 
• Situated between **60° and 65°** latitudes in both hemispheres.
 
• Formed by the convergence of warm **Westerlies** and cold **Polar Easterlies**, leading to the development of **temperate cyclones**.
 
 
 
• **Polar High Pressure Belt**:
 
 
• Located around the **North and South Poles** (80°−90°).
 
• Caused by extremely low temperatures which make the air dense, leading to constant **high pressure** and cold, dry conditions.

questions.question: Under the PM-Daksh scheme, any Other Backward Caste's (OBCs) and Economically Weaker Section (EWS) candidates whose annual family income is less than Rs. _______ lakh is eligible to get training.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalata Sampanna Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH) Yojana** is a **Central Sector Scheme** launched by the **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** in **2020-21**.
 
• The primary objective of this scheme is to increase the skill levels of the target youth by providing them **short-term** and **long-term training**, making them employable for both self-employment and wage-employment.
 
• The scheme specifically targets **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**, **Other Backward Classes (OBCs)**, **Economically Backward Classes (EBCs)**, **De-notified Tribes (DNTs)**, and **Safai Karamcharis**.
 
• According to the eligibility criteria, candidates belonging to the **Other Backward Classes (OBC)** category must have a total annual family income of less than **Rs. 3 lakh** to avail of the training benefits.
 
• For candidates under the **Economically Backward Classes (EBC)** category, the annual family income limit is even lower, stipulated at less than **Rs. 1 lakh** per annum.
 
• There is **no income limit** for candidates belonging to the **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT)**, and **Safai Karamcharis** including waste pickers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The scheme is implemented through three apex corporations under the Ministry:
 
 
• **NSFDC**: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation.
 
• **NBCFDC**: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation.
 
• **NSKFDC**: National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation.
 
 
 
• Types of Training Programs:
 
 
• **Up-skilling/Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)**: Training duration ranges from **32 to 80 hours** for artisans and sanitation workers.
 
• **Short Term Training**: Focuses on **NSQF** compliant job roles with a duration of **200 to 600 hours**.
 
• **Long Term Training**: Covers courses for **6 months to 1 year** in high-demand sectors.
 
• **Entrepreneurship Development Program (EDP)**: Aimed at youth wanting to start their own micro-enterprises, usually lasting **80 to 90 hours**.
 
 
 
• Benefits to Trainees:
 
 
• Training is provided **free of cost** to all eligible candidates.
 
• A **stipend** is provided to trainees with at least **80 percent attendance** (e.g., Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 1,500 per month depending on the category and course).

questions.question: The traditional dance style 'Gaudiya Nritya' is practiced in which of the following Indian states/ Union Territory?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaudiya Nritya** is a classical dance form that originated in the ancient region of **Gaur** (or **Gauda**), which served as the capital of **Bengal** during various historical periods.
 
• This dance form is deeply intertwined with the **Gaudiya Vaishnavism** tradition, which saw a major resurgence in the **16th century** under the spiritual leadership of **Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu**.
 
• The reconstruction and revival of **Gaudiya Nritya** as a classical discipline were spearheaded by **Dr. Mahua Mukherjee** through extensive research into the **Natya Shastra**, medieval literature, and **Pala**-**Sena** era temple sculptures.
 
• It is a composite art form that integrates elements of **temple dancing**, rhythmic **Kirtan** music, and folk traditions like **Chhau** and **Nachni**.
 
• The performance typically features themes from the **Radha-Krishna** lore and uses traditional instruments such as the **Khol** and **Kartal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Haryana**:

 
 
• Common folk dances include **Ghoomar**, **Phag**, and **Dhamal**, primarily performed during agricultural festivals like **Baisakhi**.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir**:
 
 
• Home to the **Rouf** dance, performed by women during **Ramzan**, and **Bhand Pather**, a traditional satirical folk theatre.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**:
 
 
• Best known for **Kuchipudi**, a major **Indian classical dance** recognized for its blend of **Nritta** (pure dance) and **Abhinaya** (expression).

questions.question: The "Panna Diamond Mine" is in which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Panna Diamond Mine** is located in the **Panna district** of **Madhya Pradesh** and is part of the larger **Vindhyan Range** geological formation.
 
• It is the only active, industrial-scale **diamond mine** in **India**, making **Madhya Pradesh** the leading producer of diamonds in the country.
 
• The **National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC)** is the primary public sector enterprise responsible for the mechanized mining operations at the **Majhgawan** site in **Panna**.
 
• The diamonds in this region are found in **Kimberlite pipes** and conglomerate beds, which were formed millions of years ago through volcanic and sedimentary processes.
 
• The **Panna** belt extends approximately 240 kilometers and produces various categories of diamonds, including **gem-quality**, **off-color**, and **industrial-grade** stones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jharkhand**:

 
 
• This state is the primary hub for **Coal** production in India, featuring the famous **Jharia** and **Bokaro** coalfields.
 
• It is also rich in **Iron Ore** (Singhbhum) and **Copper** (Ghatshila).
 
 
 
• **Karnataka**:
 
 
• Historically famous for **Gold** mining, particularly the **Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)** and the currently operational **Hutti Gold Mines**.
 
• It is also a major producer of **Magnetite Iron Ore** and **Manganese**.
 
 
 
• **Gujarat**:
 
 
• Renowned for its **Petroleum** and **Natural Gas** reserves located in the **Ankleshwar** and **Cambay** basins.
 
• It is the largest producer of **Salt** in India and holds significant deposits of **Lignite** and **Fluorite**.

questions.question: By which other name is the festival of Holi known in West Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dol Purnima**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **West Bengal**, the festival of **Holi** is celebrated with great fervor as **Dol Purnima** or **Dol Jatra**, marking the final full moon day of the Hindu lunar month of **Phalguna**.
 
• The festival is primarily dedicated to **Lord Krishna** and **Radha**. The deities are placed in a palanquin (the **Dol**) and carried in a procession around streets while devotees sing devotional songs and hymns.
 
• A cultural highlight of this festival is the **Basanta Utsav** (Spring Festival) held at **Shantiniketan**, a tradition established by the Nobel laureate **Rabindranath Tagore** to welcome spring through poetry, dance, and music.
 
• Participants primarily use dry colored powders known as **Abir** or **Gulal** rather than liquid colors, signifying the colors of the blossoming **Spring** (Basanta) season.
 
• This day is also of immense spiritual significance for the **Gaudiya Vaishnava** community as it marks the birth anniversary of **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu**, the **15th-century** saint who revitalized the **Bhakti movement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhai Phonta**:

 
 
• Celebrated on the second day after **Kali Puja** (Diwali) in **West Bengal**, it is the regional equivalent of **Bhai Dooj**.
 
• Sisters perform a ritual where they apply a **sandalwood paste** mark on their brothers' foreheads to pray for their protection and longevity.
 
 
 
• **Jagaddhatri Puja**:
 
 
• Dedicated to **Goddess Jagaddhatri** (the Holder of the World), this festival occurs in the month of **Kartik**, typically four days after **Durga Puja**.
 
• It is celebrated with massive community pandals, particularly in **Chandannagar** and **Krishnanagar**, featuring colossal clay idols.
 
 
 
• **Kalpataru Utsav**:
 
 
• Observed every year on **January 1st**, this festival commemorates the transformation of **Sri Ramakrishna Paramahansa** into a **Kalpataru** (wish-fulfilling tree) in **1886**.
 
• The main celebrations take place at the **Cossipore Garden House** and **Dakshineswar Kali Temple** in **Kolkata**.

questions.question: What is the change of state from liquid to gas at atmospheric pressure known as?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaporisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vaporisation** refers to the physical transition of a substance from the **liquid phase** to the **gaseous phase**.
 
• At **atmospheric pressure**, this change occurs when molecules in the liquid gain sufficient **thermal energy** to overcome the **intermolecular attractive forces** (such as hydrogen bonding or Van der Waals forces) that hold them in a condensed state.
 
• This process encompasses two distinct phenomena: **evaporation**, which is a surface-level transition occurring at any temperature, and **boiling**, which occurs throughout the bulk of the liquid at a specific **boiling point**.
 
• When a liquid reaches its boiling point at **1 atmospheric pressure** (101.325 kPa), the **vapour pressure** of the liquid becomes equal to the external atmospheric pressure.
 
• The transition requires an input of energy known as the **Latent Heat of Vaporisation**, which increases the potential energy of the particles without raising the temperature during the phase change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solidification and Freezing:**

 
 
• **Solidification** (often called **freezing**) is the phase change from **liquid to solid**.
 
• This process occurs when **kinetic energy** is removed, allowing particles to settle into a fixed, ordered **crystalline lattice** or an amorphous structure.
 
 
 
• **Deposition:**
 
 
• **Deposition** is a **thermodynamic process** where a substance transforms directly from a **gas to a solid**, bypassing the liquid state entirely.
 
• A common natural example is the formation of **sub-freezing hoar frost** on ground surfaces or the transformation of water vapour into **snow** in clouds.

questions.question: When was the gender budgeting introduced in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005-2006**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gender Budgeting** was formally introduced in India during the **Union Budget 2005-2006** under the leadership of the then Finance Minister **P. Chidambaram**.
 
• It is not a separate budget for women but a **fiscal strategy** and analytical tool used to examine the government budget through a **gender lens** to ensure equitable distribution of resources.
 
• The introduction featured the first **Gender Budget Statement**, originally known as **Statement 20** (now **Statement 13**), which disclosed the allocations specifically targeting women.
 
• The process categorizes schemes into two parts: **Part A**, which includes schemes with **100% allocation** for women, and **Part B**, which includes schemes where at least **30% of the allocation** is earmarked for women.
 
• India became one of the pioneering developing nations to institutionalize **Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB)** to address gender gaps in education, health, and economic opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Institutional Mechanisms**:

 
 
• The **Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD)** is the nodal agency for the implementation and monitoring of gender budgeting across various sectors.
 
• Following the **2005-2006** mandate, **Gender Budget Cells (GBCs)** were established within various central ministries and departments to facilitate gender-sensitive planning and evaluation.
 
• The **National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP)** provided the initial analytical framework that helped the government transition from a general budget to a gender-sensitive one.
 
 
 
• **Evolution and Background**:
 
 
• The groundwork was laid during the **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002)**, which introduced the **Women's Component Plan (WCP)** to ensure that 30% of funds from all ministries were directed toward women.
 
• In **2004**, an **Expert Group** was constituted to recommend a classification system for government expenditure to track pro-women allocations effectively.
 
• While it started with only **10 ministries** in its inaugural year, the scope of the **Gender Budget Statement** has expanded significantly, now covering over **30 ministries** and departments.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2005-2006**

questions.question: In which year did India win its first men's Cricket World Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1983**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** secured its maiden **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup** title in **1983** by defeating the formidable **West Indies**, who were the two-time defending champions.
 
• The final match was contested at the iconic **Lord's Cricket Ground** in **London** on **25th June 1983**.
 
• Under the inspirational leadership of captain **Kapil Dev**, India defended a modest total of **183 runs**, successfully bowling out the **West Indies** for **140 runs**.
 
• **Mohinder Amarnath** was adjudged the **Man of the Match** for his critical all-round performance, contributing **26 runs** and taking **3 wickets** for **12 runs**.
 
• This historic victory is widely regarded as the defining moment that transformed **cricket** into a mass obsession in **India** and shifted the game's financial center to **South Asia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1975 World Cup**:

 
 
• This was the **inaugural edition** of the tournament, officially known as the **Prudential Cup**, held in **England**.
 
• The **West Indies** won the title by defeating **Australia** in the final.
 
 
 
• **1996 World Cup**:
 
 
• Officially called the **Wills World Cup**, it was co-hosted by **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• **Sri Lanka** claimed their first championship by defeating **Australia** in the final at **Gaddafi Stadium**, Lahore.
 
 
 
• **1999 World Cup**:
 
 
• The event was primarily hosted by **England**, with secondary venues in **Scotland**, **Ireland**, **Wales**, and the **Netherlands**.
 
• **Australia** emerged victorious after defeating **Pakistan** in a one-sided final.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding Critical minerals?

I. Critical minerals are the building blocks of a modern economy.

II. Critical minerals are fast becoming the oil of the 21st century.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Critical minerals** such as **Lithium**, **Cobalt**, **Nickel**, and **Graphite** are considered the foundational components of a modern economy because they are essential for the production of advanced technologies, including **semiconductors**, **telecommunications** equipment, and **defense systems**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• As the world undergoes a massive shift from **hydrocarbons** to **green energy**, these minerals are increasingly described as the 'oil of the 21st century' because they serve as the primary fuel for the **energy transition**, powering **Electric Vehicles (EVs)** and **renewable energy** storage systems. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics and Global Significance:**

 
 
• **Definition:** A mineral is classified as 'critical' when it is essential for **economic growth** and **national security**, while its supply chain is prone to disruption due to geological scarcity or geopolitical factors.
 
• **Rare Earth Elements (REEs):** A group of 17 minerals used in **permanent magnets** for **wind turbines** and **EV motors**, currently dominated by **China** in terms of mining and processing.
 
• **Indian Context:** The **Ministry of Mines** released a list of **30 critical minerals** in 2023, including **Beryllium**, **Germanium**, and **Titanium**, to bolster the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative and secure **domestic manufacturing**.
 
• **International Alliances:** India has joined the **Mineral Security Partnership (MSP)**, a US-led initiative aimed at accelerating the development of diverse and sustainable critical energy minerals supply chains globally.
 
• **Supply Chain Vulnerability:** Unlike oil, which is traded on a liquid global market, critical minerals often have highly concentrated production sites, leading to **strategic dependencies** and the need for **bilateral trade agreements**.

questions.question: The ___ th Asian Games scheduled for Aichi-Nagoya in 2026.

• This edition was held in **Hangzhou, China**. Initially scheduled for **2022**, it was postponed to **September–October 2023** due to the global **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
 
 
• **18th Asian Games**:
 
 
• Held in **2018**, this was the first time the games were co-hosted by two cities, **Jakarta** and **Palembang**, in **Indonesia**.

• This event took place in **Incheon, South Korea**, in **2014**, featuring approximately **439 events** in **36 sports**.

• Following **Aichi-Nagoya 2026**, the **21st Asian Games** are scheduled for **Doha, Qatar**, in **2030**, and the **22nd Asian Games** will be hosted in **Riyadh, Saudi Arabia**, in **2034**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is the driving engine of the PM Gati Shakti initiative?

I. Mass Transport II. Logistics Infrastructure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass Transport** is one of the **seven engines** identified under the **PM Gati Shakti** initiative, focusing on enhancing **urban connectivity** through projects like **Metro Rail**, **Regional Rapid Transit Systems (RRTS)**, and integrated bus services to reduce congestion. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Logistics Infrastructure** is a fundamental engine designed to integrate **supply chains**, develop **Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLPs)**, and create a seamless network for the movement of goods and services across the country. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• The **PM Gati Shakti** National Master Plan is powered by a total of **seven engines**, which include **Roads**, **Railways**, **Airports**, **Ports**, **Mass Transport**, **Waterways**, and **Logistics Infrastructure**.
 
• The primary objective of these engines is to facilitate **multi-modal connectivity**, ensuring that different modes of transport are integrated to provide **last-mile connectivity** for people and goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PM Gati Shakti Master Plan**:

 
 
• Launched in **October 2021**, it is a **Rs 100 lakh crore** project aimed at holistic infrastructure development.
 
• It incorporates **16 Ministries** onto a single digital platform to ensure **synchronized planning** and avoid departmental silos.
 
• The platform was developed by **BISAG-N** (Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics) using **GIS-based** spatial planning tools.
 
• The initiative seeks to reduce India’s **logistics costs** from the current **13-14 percent** of **GDP** to approximately **8 percent**, aligning with global standards.
 
• It identifies **six pillars**: Comprehensiveness, Prioritization, Optimization, Synchronization, Analytical, and Dynamic.
 
• Key targets include increasing the **National Highway** network to **2 lakh kilometers** and creating **400 new-generation Vande Bharat trains** by **2024-25**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a stroke used in swimming?

I. Breast stroke II. Back stroke
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Breaststroke** is a swimming style in which the swimmer is on their chest and the torso does not rotate. It is characterized by simultaneous arm movements on a horizontal plane and a **frog-like kick** (whip kick). It is widely regarded as the oldest and slowest of the four competitive strokes. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Backstroke** (or back crawl) is unique because it is the only competitive stroke performed with the swimmer lying on their **back**. It involves alternating arm movements and a **flutter kick**. A key advantage of this stroke is that it allows for easy breathing, though swimmers cannot see where they are going. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***
 
• Both **Breaststroke** and **Backstroke** are officially recognized by **World Aquatics** (formerly FINA) as standard competitive disciplines in international events like the **Olympic Games** and **World Championships**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Apart from the strokes mentioned above, there are two other primary competitive swimming strokes:
 
 
• **Freestyle (Front Crawl)**:

 
 
• It is the **fastest** and most efficient swimming stroke.
 
• Characterized by an alternating overhand arm motion and a continuous **flutter kick**.
 
• Swimmers breathe by rotating their heads to the side.
 
 
 
• **Butterfly Stroke**:
 
 
• Regarded as the most **physically demanding** and technically difficult stroke.
 
• Features a simultaneous overhead arm recovery and a **dolphin kick** where the legs move together.
 
• It was developed as a variation of the breaststroke before becoming its own category in **1952**.
 
 
 
• **Individual Medley (IM)**:
 
 
• A single swimmer performs all four strokes in a specific order: **Butterfly**, **Backstroke**, **Breaststroke**, and **Freestyle**.

questions.question: Environmental Performance Index 2024 used how many performance indicators?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**58**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Environmental Performance Index (EPI) 2024** provides a data-driven summary of the state of sustainability worldwide, ranking **180 countries** on their environmental efforts.
 
• In the 2024 framework, the index utilized a total of **58 performance indicators** to provide a granular and comprehensive assessment of national environmental performance.
 
• These **58 indicators** are systematically organized into **11 issue categories**, which address specific environmental challenges such as **Air Quality**, **Biodiversity**, and **Waste Management**.
 
• The indicators are further grouped into **three overarching policy objectives**: **Climate Change**, **Environmental Health**, and **Ecosystem Vitality**.
 
• The **EPI** is a biennial report published by the **Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy** and the **Center for International Earth Science Information Network** at Columbia University.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Policy Objectives**:

 
 
• **Climate Change**: Focuses on progress toward **net-zero emissions** by 2050, tracking greenhouse gas emission growth rates and projected targets.
 
• **Environmental Health**: Evaluates factors directly impacting human well-being, including **Sanitation & Drinking Water**, **Air Quality**, and exposure to **Heavy Metals** like Lead.
 
• **Ecosystem Vitality**: Measures the health of natural systems, covering **Forestry**, **Fisheries**, **Agriculture**, and **Biodiversity & Habitat** protection.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Indicators**:
 
 
• The **58 indicators** allow for a sophisticated analysis of how close countries are to established **environmental policy targets**.
 
• By using standardized data, the **EPI** helps identify **leaders and laggards** in environmental sustainability, facilitating the sharing of best practices among nations.

questions.question: Comprehensive Environment Pollution Index in India was published by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CPCB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI)** is a framework developed to evaluate the environmental quality of **industrial clusters** and to identify areas that require immediate attention.
 
• It was designed and published by the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** in collaboration with the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Delhi** in **2009**.
 
• The primary purpose of **CEPI** is to categorize industrial clusters into **Critically Polluted Areas (CPA)**, **Severely Polluted Areas (SPA)**, and **Other Polluted Areas (OPA)** based on a scoring system.
 
• A **CEPI score** above **70** denotes a **Critically Polluted Area**, which often leads to a moratorium on new industrial activities in that region, while a score between **60 and 70** identifies a **Severely Polluted Area**.
 
• The assessment methodology considers the **scale of industrial activity**, the **nature of pollutants** (relative toxicity), the **scale of exceedance** of environmental standards, and the **impact on human health**.
 
• The index evaluates three environmental components: **Air**, **Water**, and **Land**, integrating them into a single score that reflects the overall environmental stress in a geographical area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**:

 
 
• A **statutory organization** established in **1974** under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act** to provide technical support to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**.
 
 
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT)**:
 
 
• Established on **October 18, 2010**, under the **NGT Act** for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
 
 
• **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)**:
 
 
• Operating under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, it is the national apex body responsible for managing, monitoring, and researching **groundwater resources** across India.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**:
 
 
• The **National Institution for Transforming India**, created in **January 2015** as a successor to the **Planning Commission**, serves as the premier **policy think tank** of the Indian government.
